# Introduction

We are going to perform some more quality checks and then apply some filters to remove
low quality cells 

# Libraries

```{r}
library(Signac)
library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
library(gridExtra)
library(grid)
```

# Functions

```{r}
empty_feat <- function(obj) {
  keep_genes <- data.frame(rowSums(as.matrix(obj[['RNA']]@counts)) != 0)
  colnames(keep_genes) <- "logical"
  keep_genes <- subset(keep_genes, logical==TRUE)
  obj[['RNA']]@counts <- obj[['RNA']]@counts[rownames(keep_genes), ]
  obj[['RNA']]@data <- obj[['RNA']]@data[rownames(keep_genes), ]
  return(obj)
}
```


# Parameters

```{r}
subproj <- params$subproj
patient <- params$patient

here::dr_here(show_reason = TRUE)
source(here::here(glue::glue("{subproj}/multiome_analysis/misc/paths.R")))
source(here::here("utils/bin.R"))

set.seed(0)

# filters
max_lib_size_rna <- 45000
min_lib_size_rna <- 400
max_n_genes <- 10000
min_n_genes <- 200
max_pct_mt <- 20
max_pct_ribo <- 60

TSS_enrichment <- 1 
nucleosome_signal_atac <- 2
min_frag_peak <- 1000
max_frag_peak <- 25000
fraction_read_peak <- 0.15
```

# Load data

```{r}
seurat_obj <- readRDS(here::here(glue::glue("{qc}/{robj_dir}/2.0_{patient}.rds")))
seurat_obj@meta.data$caller <- "CellRanger"
seurat_obj <- SetIdent(seurat_obj, value=seurat_obj@meta.data$caller)
```

# Apply straightforward general filters

## Filter from cross sensitivity plot 
```{r fig.height = 6, fig.width = 8, out.width = "100%"}

# these are the cut offs to apply
x_atac_cutoff <- min(seurat_obj@meta.data[seurat_obj@meta.data$is_cell == 1, "nCount_ATAC"])+10
y_rna_cutoff <- min(seurat_obj@meta.data[seurat_obj@meta.data$is_cell == 1, "nCount_RNA"])+4

# corss sensitivity plot
plot_cross_sense(seurat_obj, patient, x_atac_cutoff, y_rna_cutoff)
```

Apply this general filter before proceeding with the rest of the check metrics


```{r}
seurat_obj <- subset(x = seurat_obj,
                        nCount_ATAC > x_atac_cutoff & nCount_RNA > y_rna_cutoff)
```

## Remove empty features

```{r}
table(rowSums(as.matrix(seurat_obj[['RNA']]@counts)) == 0)
```


```{r}
seurat_obj <- empty_feat(seurat_obj)
```


## Add quality metrics too

```{r}
seurat_obj <- quality_metrics(seurat_obj)
```

# RNA

```{r}
DefaultAssay(seurat_obj) <- "RNA"
```

### Library sanity checks

The idea here is to filter any left empty droplet or lysed cells. Hinds to detect a lysed cell are:

  1. total count of UMI low ~ low library size
  2. total number of genes detected low ~ low library complexity
  3. high fraction of mitochondrial genes expression (cytosolic mRNA leaks out of the cell)

```{r}
vlp <- VlnPlot(
object = seurat_obj,
features = "nCount_RNA",
pt.size = 0.1) +  
scale_y_log10() + 
geom_hline(yintercept = max_lib_size_rna, linetype='dashed', col = 'black') +
geom_hline(yintercept = min_lib_size_rna, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
NoLegend()

hist <- plot_histogram_qc(df = seurat_obj@meta.data,
                        x = "nCount_RNA", 
                        x_lab = "Library Size (log10(total UMI))")
hist1 <- hist +
    scale_x_log10() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = max_lib_size_rna, 
              linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = min_lib_size_rna, 
              linetype = "dashed", color = "black")

hist2 <- hist +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 2000)) +
    xlab("Library Size (total UMI)") +
    theme_pubr() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = min_lib_size_rna, linetype = "dashed", color = "black")

grid.arrange(vlp, hist1, hist2, ncol=3, nrow =1,
             top = textGrob(patient, gp=gpar(fontsize=20,font=3)))

```

## Fraction of mitochondrial expression

A reasonable threshold would be to eliminate cells with a % of mitocondrial material above 20

```{r}
plt1 <- seurat_obj@meta.data %>%
plot_histogram_qc(x = "pct_mt", x_lab = "% Mitochondrial Expression") +
geom_vline(xintercept = max_pct_mt, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) 

plt2 <- ggplot(seurat_obj@meta.data, aes(x = nCount_RNA, y = nFeature_RNA, color = pct_mt)) +
  geom_point() + theme_classic() + scale_color_gradient(low = "yellow", high = "red", na.value = NA)

grid.arrange(plt1, plt2, ncol=2, nrow =1,
             top = textGrob(patient, gp=gpar(fontsize=20,font=3)))
```

## Fragment length distribution and Nucleosome signal

In Signac, to test the quality of the assay one can compute the ratio of the fragments 147 bp and 294 bp (mononucleosome) to fragments < 147 bp (nucleosome-free). This is called the nucleosome signal score and is computed per cell.

```{r}
nucleo_plot <- function(obj) {
  f <- FragmentHistogram(obj) + 
    geom_vline(xintercept  = 147, linetype='dotted', col = 'blue') +
    geom_vline(xintercept  = 294, linetype='dotted', col = 'red') +
    annotate(geom="text", x=147/2-20, y=5500, label="Nucleosome free", color="blue") +
    annotate(geom="text", x=(294-147)/2+147, y=5500, label="Mononucleosome", color="red") 

  NFR <- length(which(f$data$length < 147)) / nrow(f$data) * 100
  MONO <- length(which(f$data$length > 147 & f$data$length < 294)) / nrow(f$data) * 100
  DI <- length(which(f$data$length > 294)) / nrow(f$data) * 100
  
  f + annotate(geom="text", x = 147/2, y = 80, label = round(NFR, 2), size = 4, color="white") +
       annotate(geom="text", x = (294-147)/2+147, y = 80, label = round(MONO, 2), size = 4, color="white") +
       annotate(geom="text", x = 350, y = 80, label = round(DI, 2), size = 4, color="white")
  f + ggtitle("Fragment length distribution") +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"))
}
  
ncl <- nucleo_plot(seurat_obj)
vlp <- VlnPlot(
object = seurat_obj,
features = "nucleosome_signal",
pt.size = 0.1) +  
scale_y_log10() +
geom_hline(yintercept = nucleosome_signal_atac, linetype='dashed', 
           col = 'black') + NoLegend()

grid.arrange(ncl, vlp, ncol=2, nrow =1,
             top = textGrob(patient, gp=gpar(fontsize=20,font=3)),
             widths=c(3, 1))

```

## Transcriptional start site (TSS) enrichment score

```{r}
plot_tss <- function(obj){
 DefaultAssay(obj) <- "ATAC" 
 Signac::TSSPlot(obj, group.by = "high.tss") + 
   ggtitle("TSS enrichment score distribution")  +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"))
}

tss <- plot_tss(seurat_obj)
vlp <- VlnPlot(
object = seurat_obj,
features = "TSS.enrichment",
pt.size = 0.1) +  
scale_y_log10() +
geom_hline(yintercept = TSS_enrichment, linetype='dashed', 
           col = 'black') + scale_y_log10() + NoLegend()

grid.arrange(tss, vlp, ncol=2, nrow =1,
             top = textGrob(patient, gp=gpar(fontsize=20,font=3)))

```

# Final application of filters

```{r}
filtering_QC <- function(seurat_obj) {
  seurat_obj <- subset(
    x = seurat_obj, 
    
    #rna
    pct_mt < max_pct_mt &
    pct_ribosomal < max_pct_ribo &
    nCount_RNA > min_lib_size_rna &
    nCount_RNA < max_lib_size_rna &
    nFeature_RNA < max_n_genes &
    nFeature_RNA > min_n_genes &
   
    #atac
    atac_peak_region_fragments > min_frag_peak &
    atac_peak_region_fragments < max_frag_peak &
    FRiP > fraction_read_peak &
    nucleosome_signal < nucleosome_signal_atac &
    TSS.enrichment > TSS_enrichment)
  return(seurat_obj)
}

print("Before second filters")
print(seurat_obj)

# Apply filters
seurat_obj <- filtering_QC(seurat_obj)

print("After second filters")
print(seurat_obj)

#print("After empty features filters")
#print(seurat_obj)
```
